title: Fish with Vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender fish, baked or steamed, paired with a mix of vegetables: carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, collard greens). Salt, lemon juice and herbs add flavor, with no potatoes or soy‑based sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The fish‑and‑vegetable combination delivers a broad spectrum of nutrients in one meal.
Broccoli is rich in glucoraphanin, a compound that supports the body’s detox pathways.
Dark‑green leafy greens contain the highest amount of vitamin K of any food.
Carrots are one of the most accessible sources of beta‑carotene, a vitamin A precursor.
Steaming fish preserves most of its omega‑3 fatty acids.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish (especially fatty varieties) provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Together, fish and vegetables supply vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and carotenoids from broccoli protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: Leafy greens and broccoli add dietary fiber, calcium, iron and magnesium, aiding digestion and bone health.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: The absence of potatoes makes the dish suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury; choosing smaller fish or trusted sources reduces risk.

items.title: Excess vitamin K
items.content: People on anticoagulant medication should monitor intake of leafy greens high in vitamin K.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Lemon juice can enhance iron absorption from vegetables, but its acidity may cause discomfort for sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing fish pieces with the vegetables. Finish with fresh lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil and herbs (parsley, dill). It works as a standalone meal or as part of a larger menu.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat using a steamer or microwave to retain vegetable texture.
